about.title: Redondo Beach Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Redondo Beach runs on work you can see from the coast and work you can't: hotel and restaurant staff along the harbor, crews on office and aerospace campuses near Aviation Boulevard, and retail and warehouse teams off Artesia Boulevard. When one of those jobs leaves you hurt, the first question is rarely legal; it is how to keep paying rent in Los Angeles County while you heal. California's workers' compensation system exists for that moment, and it applies regardless of who caused the accident. Still, comp is not always the whole story. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to what happened, a separate third-party claim may be available alongside your benefits. In 2025, Redondo Beach recorded 235 injury collisions and 302 people injured, and some of those people were simply doing their jobs on Inglewood Avenue or Route 1. LawProactive is not a law firm; we connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can sort out which paths apply to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Redondo Beach Workers Start With LawProactive

items.title: Comp Benefits Don't Depend on Fault
items.desc: In California, workers' compensation is usually your exclusive remedy against your employer, and it pays regardless of who caused the accident. An attorney in our network can help you understand what that covers and what it doesn't.

items.title: A Third Party May Owe You More
items.desc: If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or another driver played a part in your injury, a separate claim against that third party may sit alongside your comp case. Sorting out who else is responsible is something an independent attorney can evaluate.

items.title: Deadlines and Protections You Should Know
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report an injury to your employer, and it is illegal for your employer to retaliate against you for doing so. Third-party injury claims carry a two-year filing deadline, so it helps to get answers early.

items.question: I was hit by another driver while making deliveries on Inglewood Avenue for my job. Do I only get workers' comp?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation should apply no matter who was at fault. But since the other driver is a third party rather than your employer, you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver. An independent attorney can review the collision report and explain how the two claims interact.

items.question: My employer cut my hours after I reported an injury. Is that allowed?
items.answer: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers for reporting a workplace injury or filing a comp claim. Reduced hours, demotion, or termination that follows a report can be a serious problem for the employer. Keep records of the timing and any communications, and bring them to the attorney you're connected with.

items.question: How long do I have to act after a workplace injury in Redondo Beach?
items.answer: Report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your workers' compensation rights. If a third party contributed to your injury, that separate claim generally must be filed within two years. Because evidence from job sites and Los Angeles County roadways can disappear quickly, earlier is better.
